messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] non wear detection vs. sleep/rest classification
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] non wear detection vs. sleep/rest classification
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mateo,
Reducing the windowsizes for non-wear detection should help to detect the shorter non-wear periods, e.g.  to 30 minutes  and 30 minutes or even less.
Note that the non-wear detection method is primarily designed to detect large windows of monitor non-wear. It is not expected to work great for very short non-wear periods. The assumption I made was that those really short non-wear periods are both not common and also have a negligible influence on the overall sleep and physical activity estimates because of their short duration.

Further worth noting is that g.part3 argument 'ignorenonwear' enables you to decide what happens with detected non-wear periods.
If TRUE (default) these are not classified as rest/sleep, but as daytime inactivity. If FALSE then these non-wear periods are likely to be classified as rest/sleep.
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of sleep visualization output?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Z,

The slashed box indicates the time that falls into the reported onset and wake-up times in your sleep log.

Green and blue boxes mean exactly the same, they are sustained inactivity bouts classified in g.part3. If these periods fall into the sleep log area, they are considered "sleep" and then colored in blue, otherwise the will be colored in green. In previous versions of GGIR, I found that for daysleepers, the boxes that should be blue were green instead, but I think this is corrected in the current GGIR version (check if you have it updated).

Otherwise, I also think that your sleep log times are wrong, do you have them in 24h format?

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] late wakeup times in sleep detection
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] late wakeup times in sleep detection
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joan,
Sorry for the late reply. Your finding seems to be in line with our paper from last year: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-31266-z. At a population level the method provides good estimates, but at an individual level measurement errors are expected.

I did not design parameters for the algorithm to tweak the waking-up time earlier later. My proposal to address the problem would be:

Do this only in the people for whom the waking up time ends after the breakfast time. Create a sleep diary (sleeplog, see GGIR documentation) where you use the breakfast time as wake-up time, and the currently estimates sleep onset time as sleep onset time.
My expectation is that this will force the algorithm to avoid estimating waking-up time after breakfast.

Further, it may be good to inspect the individual files and try to understand why the breakfast is included in the sleep period time window. For example, participant takes off the accelerometer after breakfast (e.g. during showering), participant goes back to bed after breakfast, or participant stops wearing the accelerometer because it is the last day of measurement.

Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Step counting in GGIR ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Damien,
Good suggestion and I agree that it is worth having this functionality in GGIR.

R package GENEAclassify <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GENEAclassify/index.html> implemented two step count algorithms and this works for GENEActiv accelerometers.
The GPL license that package uses is not compatible with the LGPL license used by GGIR. GGIR would either have to adopt the GPL license as per the license conditions or get explicit permission from the GENEAclassify developers to copy their code.
Changing license is not an option for me, getting permission from GENEAclassify developers is worth trying but it would not be surprise me if they say no.

One idea could be to investigate the origin of their algorithm and if it is based on an open published algorithm then use that as a starting point for implementing it in GGIR.
Another approach could be to start from scratch, develop something new, and share that with the world alongside the insights gained along the way.

Possible ways forward:
- Someone volunteers to develop this.
- Someone pays me to (co-)develop this.
Depending on the amount of work that needs to be done it may be possible to turn this into a student project.

Best regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: GGIR release 1.8-1
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

GGIR version 1.8-1 is now online, as always the changes are recorded in the change log: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html. The 1.8-0 in this list is a typo, because there is no version 1.8-0 (I will fix that next time).

Key changes:
- Improvements to file reading functionality for .cwa-format AX3 (Axivity) files: Previously files were sometimes not entirely loaded due to a bug, which is now addressed.
- A range of bug fixes that probably have no major impact on study results, but still valuable for enhancing the quality of GGIR (see change log).

Acknowledgements:
For this release I would like to thank Evgeny Mirkes (Leicester) and Joan Capdevila Pujol (Barcelone) who fixed some of the bugs and provided constructive feedback that helped me to improve parts of the GGIR code.

Best wishes, Vincent

messages.subject: Exploration for GGIR workshop potential
messages.body_plain:
Hi GGIR users,

I have been receiving questions about when I will be giving a GGIR workshop. I am quite busy, but if there is a lot of interest then there must be a way to organise it. Possibly with the help from some GGIR contributors and/or experienced users. So, let's explore this.

If you are interested in a GGIR workshop, then please respond to this message with your answers to the following questions:

Content:
1. Are you interested in lectures by me (and optionally other GGIR contributors) about what GGIR can do and how it works? yes/no
2. Are you interested in a basic introduction about R? yes/no
3. Are you interested in hands-on working together on real data with GGIR? yes/no
4. Are you interested in learning how you can contribute to GGIR with GitHub? yes/no
5. Are you interested in discussions about accelerometer data analysis in general to guide future GGIR developments? yes/no
6. Are you interested in a mini-hackaton to work on GGIR together? yes/no
7. If you responded yes to more than one of the above, what would be the ideal balance for you?

Organisation:
8. Are you able to host the workshop and help minimise the organisational burden for me? yes/no. Here, it would be helpful for me if my expenses can be covered either by the hosting organisation or by workshop participants.
9. Are you interested in co-organising the workshop by taking responsibility for a part of the workshop?

Your needs:
10. Is there a specific week or date you would like the workshop to take place?
11. How much are you willing to pay as participation fee per person for a one-day workshop, including lunch and coffee?
12. How much are you willing to pay as participation fee per person for a two-day workshop, including lunch, coffee and one dinner, excluding accommodation?
13. In what country, state/province, and city are you based?
14. How far are you willing to travel for the workshop? only within same city; only within same state/province; only within same nation; or only within same continent.
15. How many people do you expect to be able to enlist for the workshop, including yourself?
16. Do you have any comments/suggestions?

Your responses to the above questions will hopefully give me some idea of what could be a viable plan.

Thanks,
Vincent

messages.subject: Daily log in GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent and all GGIR users,

Firstly, thank you for amazing work. I am responsible for accelerometer-data processing at our department.

We use regularly about 400 ActiGraphs and 70 Axivity. I went over some issues with GGIR regarding to date-format, character used to separate decimals etc (mostly based on eastern Europe

settings of windows). Now, I am using it with no errors at all, and I'm very happy with that. I just would like to ask three questions:

1. Is there (or will be soon) any chance to use "daily log" with timetable to separate outcomes of physical activity for specific time-period (e.g. before-school, in-school, after-school, during PE lessons...)?

2. Is there any way to translate labels into Czech language in participant's feedback? We would like to provide it to children and not all of them are good in English.

3. Is there in GGIR community an agreement of mg threshold for classifying moderate physical activity among children (for ActiGraph, non-dominant wrist)? It is 201.4 mg based on Hildebrand et al. 2014? For Czech children, it seems to be to high :D.

Note: I am a complete beginner in R, the GGIR was a reason why I recently installed it.

Thank you.

Jan Dygryn,

Institute of Active Lifestyle

Palacký University Olomouc, Czech Republic.

> We use regularly about 400 ActiGraphs and 70 Axivity. I went over some issues with GGIR regarding to date-format, character used to separate decimals etc (mostly based on eastern Europe
>
> settings of windows). Now, I am using it with no errors at all, and I'm very happy with that. I just would like to ask three questions:
>
> 1. Is there (or will be soon) any chance to use "daily log" with timetable to separate outcomes of physical activity for specific time-period (e.g. before-school, in-school, after-school, during PE lessons...)?
>
> 2. Is there any way to translate labels into Czech language in participant's feedback? We would like to provide it to children and not all of them are good in English.
>
>
>
> 3. Is there in GGIR community an agreement of mg threshold for classifying moderate physical activity among children (for ActiGraph, non-dominant wrist)? It is 201.4 mg based on Hildebrand et al. 2014? For Czech children, it seems to be to high :D.
>
>
> Note: I am a complete beginner in R, the GGIR was a reason why I recently installed it.
>
>
>
> Thank you.
>
>
>
> Jan Dygryn,
>
> Institute of Active Lifestyle
>
> Palacký University Olomouc, Czech Republic.
